changed.what: The record used the retired schema `frob.pilot/1` and an entry name the register's loader rejects. It is now a `frob.gauntlet.pilot/1` record in crates/frob-conformance/registry/pilots.toml (proposed PILOT-KIN-10, with mechanism, tier, protocol hash, the three falsifiers, ceiling, fallback and KILL-LOOPELIM, integrated gate), registered before the run; dep N38a-09. The e2e paragraph gives the exact commands of the out-of-workspace prototype and the census file. The f32 arm of the prototype now evaluates the closed form as the kernels must (unit complex, no trigonometry), or its residual would predict nothing.

Two gaps. (1) Nobody owned the switch that keeps every closure a row, although `--closures rows`, the gate's comparison and KILL-LOOPELIM's fallback need it and the compiler does the marking: added the compile input `closure_policy` (auto | rows), reason `policy`, acceptance and test. (2) Dependent joints are unit complex numbers with turn counters recomputed each step; the sign-only crossing rule that updates a counter is valid only below a quarter turn per step, so a loop is now eliminated only if a/(c·s_min) and 1 + a/(b·s_min) are at most 7 (reason `ratio-too-large`), with hand-checked cases (0.605 and 1.504 pass; 18.6 is refused). Known answers cite the four N16-KA slugs.

The kernels could not be built as written: they called `det_atan2`, `det_sin` and `det_cos`, which no bead registers (N21a-11's set has none, and an unregistered det function is a build error), and took an angle although the batched state stores a revolute coordinate as a unit complex number and admits no trigonometry in a kernel. Restated in a trigonometry-free unit-complex form (inputs e(θ), outputs e(φ), e(ψ); ratios from products of components), verified numerically against every known answer and derived check value on both branches. The earlier 'better conditioned' atan2(sin β, cos β) form also missed the bead's own f32 bound (4.2e-6 m, 0.05% of 10⁶ random admissible linkages above 1e-6 m, because sin β = b·sin μ/R); the half-angle form from side lengths stays below 4e-7 m. Added the pinned short-coupler case, the `direct-cosine` mutant, the dependent joints' turn counters with a crank-rocker test, and keys on spark.check. Deps: N21a-11 replaced by N21a-16 and BD-157.

`--closures` was used but never defined: now `sim.run --closures auto|rows` (default auto, echoed in the receipt, bad value 802), passing N16c-30's closure policy; dep N16b-25 (the verb it extends, not reachable before). The reflected-inertia sentence could be read backwards; restated from ΓᵀAΓ. The refusal of a per-world variant that enters the toggle guard or breaks the ratio bound had no message, repairs, block or exit: specified, with a hand-checked test (b = 1.2 fails above 87.2°). Stage 1 states the stored form of the dependent coordinates. K-loop-reduce added to the e2e kernel check.

`--test g1` and `--test g2` are not targets: now g1_known_answers and g2_parity with FROB_TEST_SEED, the mutation feature for the controls, and record_gate by the reviewing session. Every compared sim.run carries its own --key. Added the `kernels` step (spark.check on the three four-bar kernels and K-loop-reduce) and the energy-ledger metric that N16c-31 and N16c-32 say this script carries; the `hold-<deg>` task variants that prescribe θ; φ formed on the host from the unit complex and turn counter; n asserted at the kernel level, since it is not state; the registered controls by name. Dep N16-KA.

Decision record moved from 'ADR-KIN-17' to docs/adr/ADR-KILL-LOOPELIM-M2.md with N40-03's required fields and the gates.toml `decision` table; pilot input named by its register record; the kill state is the compiler's closure policy fixed to rows. notes: Unchanged: N16c-35, N21a-05, N21a-09, N21a-12, N21a-19, N21a-22, N33a-21 (read in full; their arithmetic recomputed and correct). Round 1 left the mathematics of the slice sound: every count, known answer and canary I recomputed holds. What it left were convention drifts (test target names, keys, pilot and decision records, the tier split of the overflow refusal), commands that no verb offers, and three real design gaps in the loop-elimination chain: kernels written against trigonometric functions that do not exist in a design that stores angles as unit complex numbers, a single-precision bound the stated formulation misses, and no owner for the rows-only switch or for the dependent joints' turn counters. The slice should settle once the registry rows requested above exist; N16c-30 to N16c-33 deserve one more read in round 3 because their fixes are substantive.
